content_preview.title: Rust 1.99 Stabilizes C-Variadic Function Definitions and Raw-Pointer Layout Queries, and Disables Cargo Incremental Builds in CI
content_preview.summary: Rust 1.99.0, released October 1, lets developers define C-ABI variadic functions in Rust, stabilizes raw-pointer size and alignment functions, and changes Cargo defaults.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The Rust Release Team announced Rust 1.99.0 on October 1, 2026, according to the [Rust Blog](https://blog.rust-lang.org/2026/10/01/Rust-1.99.0/). The release's headline feature is the stabilization of C-ABI variadic function definitions, which means functions that take a variable argument list can now be written in Rust itself. Developers with a rustup installation can update with `rustup update stable`, per the same announcement.

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured 585-word News piece (range 400-1200) with Overview, What Changed, Cargo/Tooling, Compatibility Notes and a What We Don't Know section. Neutral, no AI self-reference, no code examples reproduced, so no code-exactness risk; all API names match the sources.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read source-0.html.gz (Rust Blog 'Announcing Rust 1.99.0', Oct. 1, 2026, The Rust Release Team) in full: confirms release date, rustup update stable, C-ABI variadic definitions with "C" and "C-unwind", quote 'these functions can now be written in Rust itself' (verbatim: 'With Rust 1.99, these functions can now be written in Rust itself'), VaList / VaArgSafe, naked variadic functions via inline assembly, Layout::for_value_raw / mem::size_of_val_raw / mem::align_of_val_raw, Box::leak guidance (Box::into_non_null or Box::into_raw, applies to other leak functions, custom allocators), and the full stabilized-API list incl. VecDeque::retain_back, Vec::into_parts/from_parts, String::from_utf8_lossy_owned, fs::set_times(_nofollow), IntoIterator for Box<[T; N]>. All confirmed. Read source-1.html.gz (github.com RELEASES.md): the snapshot is GitHub's React-rendered page whose rich text is truncated (richTextTruncated:true); it contains the 1.99.0 entry only as table-of-contents headings ('Version 1.99.0 (2026-10-01)', Cargo, Rustdoc, Compatibility Notes, Internal Changes), NOT the entry body, so the Cargo/rustdoc/platform/compat claims could not be verified from the snapshot. Per the instruction to use the live URL only as a last resort, the same file was fetched live from raw.githubusercontent.com/rust-lang/rust/main/RELEASES.md (recorded here as a live-URL fallback, not the snapshot) and the 1.99.0 section read: 'In Cargo, incremental compilation is now disabled by default when running in CI. CI is detected via the `CI` environment variable.' (listed under Compatibility Notes); new built-in `debug` profile with 'Currently there is no difference between `dev` and `debug` profiles'; edition-2024 default-features override, 'ignored with a warning' on earlier editions; rustdoc 'performance improvements of 20% on average and up to 40%'; riscv64-unknown-linux-musl Tier 2 with host tools; LLVM 23; legacy integral modules fully deprecated; no_mangle_generic_items hard error. All body claims confirmed. suspicious_patterns was null for both sources; nothing to evaluate. blog.rust-lang.org and github.com are both in config/source_allowlist.txt.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Body is accurate to the sources. The one precision issue is the headline: it says the release 'Disables Cargo Incremental Builds in CI'. The release notes say incremental compilation is disabled BY DEFAULT when running in CI, detected via the CI environment variable. It is a changed default, not an unconditional removal of incremental builds. The article body states this correctly; only the headline omits 'by default'. The summary ('changes Cargo defaults') is accurate. Also minor: the article calls C-variadics 'the headline feature'; the blog lists it first but does not use that wording.
editor_notes.originality: No existing article covers Rust 1.99.0 (grep of articles for 'Rust 1.99' / '1.99.0' / 'c-variadic' returns only the August Rust-team rustdoc piece and an unrelated 1.97.1 article). Previous release coverage is Rust 1.98.0 (Aug 21); this is a new release.
concerns: Headline says Cargo incremental builds are disabled in CI without 'by default'; the source describes a default change keyed on the CI environment variable.
The RELEASES.md snapshot does not contain the 1.99.0 entry body (truncated GitHub rendering); Cargo and other release-note claims were verified against the live raw file instead.
recommendations: Publish a clarification that the Cargo change is a default, not a removal.
Prefer raw.githubusercontent.com or the tagged release-notes URL for long GitHub-rendered markdown files so the snapshot contains the entry.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Substantively accurate, well-sourced, primary-source article. A single clarification covers the headline imprecision; APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS.
